name: Vectoria
summary: A talking pixel-art expert on Vector bots and WebXDC: !vec answers in text, !vectoria in a lip-synced video.
description:
Vectoria knows the Vector SDKs (Python, Rust, JS) and WebXDC Mini Apps, and searches the web when her notes don't cover something. Ask with !vec for a text answer (code included), or !vectoria for a short video: her sprite lip-syncs to a retro SAM voice under a VHS filter, with C64-style subtitles. Reply to any of her answers to keep talking. She remembers each person (!vecmemory, !vecforget), and 👍/👎 votes are kept.

Needs: an Ollama API key (ollama.com, free tier works) in the bot's .env as OLLAMA_API_KEY, or a local Ollama. For videos: ffmpeg, plus her voice, which an owner builds once with !vecvoice (git and a C compiler). Without those she still answers in text. This module runs Python, so it needs Settings → Marketplace → Allow modules with code.
author: lucky-edgelord

files.kb_vector_miniapps.md:
# Mini Apps in Vector
Vector runs WebXDC-compatible Mini Apps in isolated webviews, compatible with Delta Chat. Apps are .xdc files. Sandbox: no network access (no HTTP or WebSocket), strict CSP allowing only self, data and blob URLs, WebRTC disabled to prevent IP leaks, and a permission system for sensitive APIs. Apps are identified by the SHA-256 hash of the file, not by a name the author controls.

# Vector Nexus and the marketplace
The in-app Mini App store is Vector Nexus. It is a decentralized marketplace built on Nostr and Blossom: listings are Nostr events of kind 30078 (parameterized replaceable application-specific data) with metadata tags, the .xdc files are hosted on Blossom, and downloads are verified by SHA-256. A trusted publisher key (the Vector project) is shown first and users can add custom publishers. Listings can be edited only by their publisher.

# Permissions
Apps can request permissions such as camera, microphone, screen capture, speaker selection, geolocation, clipboard read and write, accelerometer, gyroscope, magnetometer, light sensor, Bluetooth, MIDI, fullscreen, autoplay, picture in picture and screen wake lock. Users see a prompt on first launch and can toggle each one in App Details. Enforcement is by Permissions-Policy headers plus JavaScript API wrapping, and permissions persist per file hash.

# Bridge API in Vector
webxdc.selfAddr is the user's npub, webxdc.selfName the display name. setUpdateListener and sendUpdate sync persisted state to chat participants. joinRealtimeChannel gives a low-latency peer to peer channel with messages up to 128 KB.

# Realtime multiplayer
Realtime uses Iroh gossip (QUIC). When a user taps start multiplayer the app calls joinRealtimeChannel, which advertises the peer over Nostr; others who open the same app in the same chat join. The topic is minted once when the .xdc is sent and carried on the file event as a webxdc-topic tag so every participant joins the same topic. Direct IPs are stripped from advertisements but Iroh relays see peer IPs, and players in a session can see each other's IPs. Compatible with Delta Chat's realtime implementation.

# Example: DOOM
VectorPrivacy/DOOM is a fork of Cloudflare's doom-wasm with networking rebuilt for WebXDC realtime channels: no server, host auto-elected by magic-byte election in about 3 seconds, position snapshots every 57 ms with interpolation, host-authoritative damage and NPCs, late join, touch controls, a 4.2 MB .xdc. Find it in Vector Nexus under Multiplayer.
files.kb_vector_platform.md:
# Vector in short
Vector is a private, encrypted messenger built on Nostr, with desktop and mobile apps built on the vector-core engine (Tauri). Website vectorapp.io, source github.com/VectorPrivacy/Vector. Default relays include wss://jskitty.cat/nostr, wss://asia.vectorapp.io/nostr, wss://nostr.computingcache.com and wss://relay.damus.io; relay settings are customizable with live metrics. DMs use NIP-17 gift wraps.

# Communities
Vector v0.4.0 is the Communities release. Communities have channels, roles, permission overwrites, modes and invite links (vectorapp.io/invite/... links hold an naddr plus a key). Communities are built on the Concord protocol. Bots join with invite links via client.join(url) in vector-sdk-py.

# Invites
A Community invite link looks like https://vectorapp.io/invite/naddr1...#<key>. The part after # is the key. Anyone with the full link can join, so treat it as a secret for private communities.

# Where to look
Docs: vector-privacy.gitbook.io/vector-privacy (SDK page, Communities, Concord protocol). Rust SDK: docs.rs/vector_sdk and github.com/VectorPrivacy/Vector-SDK. Python SDK: github.com/lucky-edgelord/vector-sdk-py. WebXDC spec: webxdc.org/docs/spec.
files.kb_vector_sdk_py.md:
# vector-sdk-py overview
vector-sdk-py is an unofficial community discord.py-style Python library for Vector messenger bots, powered by the official Rust vector_sdk compiled in with PyO3. Same decorators, cogs, ctx, checks, cooldowns, converters, wait_for, tasks.loop, embeds and views as discord.py. Install: pip install git+https://github.com/lucky-edgelord/vector-sdk-py. It compiles Rust, so you need rustup and cmake (for the Opus voice codec). Python 3.9+ with an abi3 wheel. Optional features: whisper (speech to text), tor, i2p via --config-settings=build-args="--features whisper,tor". Voice and Mini Apps are built by default.

# Minimal bot
import vector
from vector.ext import commands
bot = commands.Bot(command_prefix="!")
@bot.event
async def on_ready(): print(f"Logged in as {bot.user}")
@bot.command()
async def ping(ctx): await ctx.reply("pong")
bot.run(os.environ.get("VECTOR_NSEC"))
Commands also appear in Vector's / picker with typed args. Default prefix is "/", set "!" to accept text commands too. Load cogs in setup_hook so they are in the manifest published at startup.

# Keys
A Vector identity is a Nostr key; bot.run(nsec) works like a Discord token. vector.generate_nsec() makes one. bot.run() with no key reuses the key stored in data_dir (default ./vector-bot-data) and creates one on first run. bot.run(mnemonic="...") takes a seed phrase.

# discord.py mapping
Guild is Community (Guild is an alias). user.id is user.npub (id is an alias); ids are strings (npub or 64-char hex), so use TEXT columns not INTEGER. Intents are accepted and ignored. hybrid_command, group, Cog.listener, load_extension (async def setup(bot)), checks, has_permissions, cooldown, is_owner (owner_id takes an npub), converters, vector.Embed (rendered as coloured markdown), vector.ui View/Button/Select/Modal (built from reactions), app_commands CommandTree (sync is a no-op), tasks.loop, VoiceChannel.connect and vc.play(FFmpegPCMAudio). message.delete deletes your own, hides others. delete_after sets a NIP-40 expiry. ephemeral=True sends a DM. Discord-only classes are stubs raising vector.NotSupportedOnVector.

# Events
on_ready, on_message, on_message_edit, on_message_delete, on_reaction_add/remove, on_raw_reaction_add/remove, on_typing, on_member_join/remove/update, on_member_ban/unban, on_guild_join/remove, on_command_error and more. Vector extras: on_community_invite (await invite.accept() with invite_policy="manual"), on_community_change, on_member_kick, on_member_timeout, on_channel_keyed, on_community_dissolve, on_xdc_presence, on_xdc_session, on_slash_command.

# Communities and messages
Communities: create_community, join(invite_url), fetch_invite, guild.create_invite(max_age, label), roles, channels (text, voice, forum, category), permission overwrites, pins, audit_logs, bans, timeouts, nicknames, relay management. Messages: history() pulls older pages from relays, edit, replies, custom emoji packs via bot.subscribe_emoji_pack(naddr), attachments via await attachment.read(), typing, expires_in. Account: bot.user.edit(username=, avatar=, about=), block/unblock, change_presence. Anything unwrapped is at bot.native (the raw Rust bot).

# Mini Apps from Python
@bot.xdc_app("vector-counter") (or "*" for any app) async def handler(session): async for event in session: if event.type == "data": await session.send_json({...}). Event types: data, peer_join, peer_leave. event.verified_sender is the one to trust. await channel.send_xdc("app.xdc") shares an app; message.xdc.join() and .manifest() work on shared ones.

# Known issues
One bot per process (the Rust SDK is process-global; a second Client raises ClientException). Reply ordering: Vector sorts by whole-second timestamps, so replies wait briefly until the clock passes the incoming message second; disable with Client(reply_ordering=False). Also included: BDScript engine (vector-bdscript), aoi.js-style interface, Discord-compatible webhooks server (vector-webhooks).
files.kb_vector_sdk_rust.md:
# vector_sdk (Rust)
vector_sdk is the official ergonomic Rust library for bots on Vector, a private encrypted messenger built on Nostr. It is a thin layer over the vector-core engine used by the desktop and mobile apps. SDK v0.3 targets Vector v0.4.0 and later. Crate: vector_sdk on crates.io, docs at docs.rs/vector_sdk.

# Quick start
let bot = VectorBot::builder().nsec("nsec1...").build().await?; bot.on_message(|_bot, msg| async move { if msg.is_mine() { return; } let _ = msg.reply("hi").await; }).await?; Handles DMs and communities with one API: a Channel works the same for both. Auto-reconnects and catches up on missed messages. One bot per process.

# Channel API
channel.send, reply(msg_id, text), react(msg_id, emoji), react_custom, typing(), edit, delete, send_file(path); bot.download_attachment, save_attachment. Get channels with bot.channel(id), bot.dm(npub) or msg.channel(). Incoming message: msg.reply, msg.react, msg.is_mine(), msg.text(), msg.member(), msg.community(), attachments on msg.message.attachments.

# Communities
member.kick/ban/unban/grant_admin/revoke_admin/is_admin; bot.community(id).invite(npub), create_invite(), members(), edit(name, description), leave(), dissolve() (owner only). Accept invites with builder .public() (anyone) or .whitelist([npubs]); otherwise handle bot.pending_invites() and bot.accept_invite(id).

# Events and profiles
bot.on_event handles BotEvent: Message, MessageUpdate (reaction or edit), deletes, MemberJoin, member leave, typing, invites, removed from community. Profiles: fetch_profile, cached_profile, update_profile, set_status, block, unblock, set_nickname, upload_image. Bots are tagged as bots automatically.

# Accounts
No key: build() creates an identity on first run and reuses it (give each bot its own .data_dir). .nsec(), .mnemonic(), .password() for encrypted keys, VectorBot::generate_nsec(). Optional Tor with the tor feature plus .tor(); I2P as well. Escape hatch: bot.core() for the full VectorCore.

# Mini Apps in the Rust SDK (xdc module)
A bot can join a Mini App's realtime channel: bot.xdc("app-id").run(|bot, mut session| async move { while let Some(event) = session.next().await { if let XdcEvent::Data(frame) = event { let msg: Value = frame.json().unwrap_or_default(); session.send_json(&json!({...})).await; } } }). Match by manifest id, by hash, or "*" (no download). Matching reads the app manifest by downloading it once, up to download_limit (default 32 MiB). XdcFrame::from says who sent; verified_sender is the one to act on. The bot's selfAddr is its npub. Messages are up to 128000 bytes, nothing is stored, so greet newcomers with state and resend whole state after changes. Sessions started by run end when the handler returns, after 3 minutes without anyone connected (idle_timeout) or 15 minutes with no message (quiet_timeout); Xdc::join sessions last until dropped. Players see each other's IPs, and a bot on Tor or I2P stays out unless allow_outside_transport. Use cases: opponent, referee, or the server behind an app that needs more than a phone (an LLM, a database).
files.kb_webxdc.md:
# WebXDC basics
WebXDC is a format for mini apps shared in a chat. An app is a ZIP file with the extension .xdc. The ZIP must use Deflate or Store compression and must contain index.html. It may contain manifest.toml, icon.png or icon.jpg. Each device runs its own copy of the app when the recipient taps Start. Apps are network-isolated, so no HTTP requests or WebSockets; they share state only through the webxdc API.

# WebXDC manifest and icon
manifest.toml sits in the zip root. Fields: name (the app name; if missing the file name is used) and source_code_url (optional link to the source). Vector's SDK also reads an id field in the manifest (for example id = "vector-counter") so a bot can match apps by id. The icon should be square, 128 to 512 pixels; do not add rounded corners, the messenger does that.

# webxdc.js
Add <script src="webxdc.js"></script> to index.html. Do not put webxdc.js in the .xdc file: the messenger provides it. To test in a browser use the webxdc-dev tool or the webxdc.js from the Hello example app.

# sendUpdate
window.webxdc.sendUpdate(update, descr). The update is sent to all peers and the sender also receives it in the listener. update.payload can be any JSON value (not undefined; binary must be base64). Optional fields: info (short chat message, about 50 chars, use sparingly), href (relative URL to open when someone taps the info message), document (document name, about 20 chars, only for apps that edit documents), summary (short text beside the icon like "8 votes", about 20 chars), notify (map of address to notification text, "*" is a catch-all). descr is deprecated, pass an empty string. If you call it too often updates get delayed: default sendUpdateInterval is 10000 ms and sendUpdateMaxSize is 128000 bytes. Batch changes and chunk big data.

# setUpdateListener
let promise = window.webxdc.setUpdateListener((update) => {}, serial). The callback runs for updates sent by you and by peers. serial is the last serial you already know (default 0). The promise resolves when all known updates were processed. Each update has payload, serial, max_serial (when serial equals max_serial this is the newest update), info, href, document, summary, notify. Call it once only: calling it several times is undefined behavior and only the last one works. Keep state derivable from the sequence of updates, since every peer replays them.

# selfAddr and selfName
webxdc.selfAddr is the user's address (in Vector it is their npub) and webxdc.selfName their display name.

# sendToChat
window.webxdc.sendToChat({file:{name, blob|base64|plainText}, text}) prepares a message the user can send to a chat; the user may edit or cancel and the app is not told. It may exit the app. Use plainText for text files rather than btoa, which breaks on emoji. Errors reject the promise.

# importFiles
let files = await window.webxdc.importFiles({extensions:[".ics"], mimeTypes:["text/calendar"], multiple:false}). Returns an array of File objects. Extensions start with a dot. Specifying a mimeType means you should also list the extensions.

# Realtime channel
const ch = window.webxdc.joinRealtimeChannel(); ch.setListener((data) => {}) receives Uint8Array items; ch.send(uint8array) sends up to 128000 bytes; ch.leave() leaves. It is experimental: check window.webxdc.joinRealtimeChannel !== undefined. Channels are private to the chat, isolated per app, and ephemeral: data only reaches peers connected right now, nothing is stored and delivery is not guaranteed, so send whole state after changes and greet newcomers with the current state. Joining twice without leaving throws.

# Packaging a .xdc
Zip the files with index.html at the root: zip -9 -r app.xdc index.html manifest.toml icon.png *.js *.css. Keep it small; chat messages carry the file. Test with webxdc-dev before sharing.

# State patterns
Because updates are replayed by every peer, treat the update list as an event log. Use serial to catch up, keep your own state in memory built from updates, and use info messages sparingly. For games with fast input use the realtime channel for movement and sendUpdate for results that must persist.
files.persona.md:
You are Vectoria, a pixel-art girl in a green gaming headset and a black hoodie with glowing green stripes, glasses on, hair pulled into long black and green twin tails. You are an expert on Vector, the private Nostr-based messenger, its bot SDKs (vector-sdk-py, the Rust vector_sdk, vector-sdk-js) and WebXDC mini apps. You live in the community "{community}" and help people build bots and Mini Apps.

Personality:
- Calm, upbeat and a little nerdy. You like clean APIs and working examples. You get quietly excited when someone ships something.
- You are honest about what you don't know. If you aren't sure, say so and look it up rather than guessing.

Facts:
- When "Notes" are included below, they are facts you can trust; use them. When a question is about something recent, a specific library version, or anything the notes don't cover, use web_search and then web_fetch the best page before you answer. Never invent function names, parameters or links.
- When you used the web, say where the answer came from in a few words, like "according to the webxdc spec".

Memory:
- You may be given notes about this person from earlier conversations. Use them naturally without announcing that you have notes.

Boundaries:
- Stay friendly and SFW. Never claim to be a real person. Never repeat or ask for anyone's secret keys (nsec) or API keys; if someone pastes one, tell them to rotate it.

"""Vectoria's voice and face: SAM speaks each line, her sprite lip-syncs to it, then a VHS pass and C64 subtitles.

Ported from the standalone Vectoria bot (itself a port of Neku's ``avatar_waifu``), without numpy or NLTK: everything
here is Pillow (already part of Vectiq), the standard library, ffmpeg and SAM.

SAM (https://github.com/s-macke/SAM) has no licence file, so it is never bundled: :func:`build_sam` clones and
compiles it on the bot's computer when an owner asks (``!vecvoice`` or the dashboard), like Vectoria's installer did.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import base64
import io
import json
import math
import os
import random
import re
import shutil
import subprocess
import tempfile
from array import array
from datetime import timedelta
from pathlib import Path

from PIL import Image, ImageDraw, ImageFilter

HERE = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
FRAME_NAMES = ("open_closed", "open_talk", "blink_closed", "blink_talk")
SAMPLE_RATE = 22050
FPS = 24
AUDIO_KBPS = 40  # SAM is 22 kHz mono: it needs very little
SAM_REPO = "https://github.com/s-macke/SAM"

#: libass style for the burned-in subtitles: pale phosphor green on a black outline, like a C64 screen
SUBTITLE_STYLE = (
    "FontName=Press Start 2P,FontSize=12,Bold=0,PrimaryColour=&H00C8FFD2,OutlineColour=&H00000000,"
    "BackColour=&H80000000,BorderStyle=1,Outline=1.2,Shadow=0,Alignment=2,MarginV=12,Spacing=0.3"
)


class RenderError(Exception):
    """The voice or the video couldn't be made (the reply falls back to text)."""


def _run(cmd: list, **kw) -> subprocess.CompletedProcess:
    try:
        p = subprocess.run(cmd, capture_output=True, **kw)
    except FileNotFoundError as e:
        raise RenderError(f"{cmd[0]} is not installed") from e
    except subprocess.TimeoutExpired as e:
        raise RenderError(f"{cmd[0]} took too long") from e
    if p.returncode != 0:
        raise RenderError(f"{Path(cmd[0]).name} failed: {p.stderr.decode(errors='replace')[-400:]}")
    return p


# -- text -----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
_SENTENCE = re.compile(r"(?<=[.!?…])\s+")
_ABBREV = re.compile(r"(\b(e\.g|i\.e|etc|vs|mr|mrs|ms|dr|st|no|approx)\.|\b[A-Za-z]\.)$", re.I)


def sentences(text: str) -> list:
    """Sentences, one thought per line: a line break always ends one. "e.g.", "Mr." and the like don't."""
    out = []
    for line in re.split(r"\n+", text.strip()):
        parts = []
        for piece in _SENTENCE.split(line.strip()):
            if parts and _ABBREV.search(parts[-1]):
                parts[-1] += " " + piece
            elif piece.strip():
                parts.append(piece.strip())
        out += parts
    return out


def trim_spoken(text: str, max_sentences: int = 3, max_chars: int = 240) -> str:
    """Short enough for a short video: the first sentences, within ``max_chars``."""
    out, used = [], 0
    for s in sentences(text):
        if len(out) >= max_sentences or (out and used + len(s) > max_chars):
            break
        out.append(s)
        used += len(s) + 1
    spoken = " ".join(out) or text.strip()
    if len(spoken) > max_chars:
        cut = max(spoken.rfind(", ", 0, max_chars), spoken.rfind(" ", 0, max_chars))
        spoken = spoken[: cut if cut > max_chars // 3 else max_chars].rstrip(" ,;:") + "."
    return spoken


def split_lines(text: str, max_chars: int = 80) -> list:
    """Spoken lines (one subtitle each): sentences, with long ones broken at a comma or a space."""
    lines = []
    for s in sentences(text):
        while len(s) > max_chars:
            cut = max(s.rfind(", ", 0, max_chars), s.rfind(" ", 0, max_chars))
            cut = cut if cut > max_chars // 3 else max_chars
            lines.append(s[: cut + 1].strip())
            s = s[cut + 1:].strip()
        if s:
            lines.append(s)
    return lines


# -- the voice: SAM -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
_SAY = [
    (r"```.*?```", " "), (r"https?://\S+", "link"), (r"`+", ""), (r"[*_#>~|]+", ""),
    (r"\bwebxdc\b", "web ex dee cee"), (r"\bxdc\b", "ex dee cee"), (r"\bnpub\b", "en pub"), (r"\bnsec\b", "en sec"),
    (r"\bsdk\b", "ess dee kay"), (r"\bapi\b", "ay pee eye"), (r"\bjs\b", "jay ess"), (r"\bnostr\b", "nostur"),
    (r"&", " and "), (r"@", " at "), (r"%", " percent "), (r"\+", " plus "), (r"=+", " equals "), (r"[/\\]", " "),
    (r"[‘’]", "'"), (r"[“”]", '"'), (r"[–—]", ", "), (r"…", "..."),
]


def sayable(text: str, limit: int = 250) -> str:
    """SAM reads plain ASCII only, 254 characters at most."""
    for pattern, repl in _SAY:
        text = re.sub(pattern, repl, text, flags=re.I | re.S)
    text = re.sub(r"[^A-Za-z0-9 .,?!'\-:;]", " ", text.encode("ascii", "ignore").decode("ascii"))
    text = re.sub(r"\s+", " ", text).strip()
    if len(text) > limit:
        cut = max(text.rfind(". ", 0, limit), text.rfind(", ", 0, limit), text.rfind(" ", 0, limit))
        text = text[: cut if cut > limit // 3 else limit].rstrip(" ,;:")
    return text


def sam_home(data_dir: str) -> Path:
    return Path(data_dir) / "vectoria" / "SAM"


def find_sam(configured: str, data_dir: str) -> str | None:
    """The SAM binary: the configured path, the one built in the data folder, ``$SAM_BIN``, or ``sam`` on PATH."""
    for c in (configured, str(sam_home(data_dir) / "sam"), os.environ.get("SAM_BIN", "")):
        if c and os.path.isfile(c) and os.access(c, os.X_OK):
            return c
    return shutil.which("sam")


def build_sam(data_dir: str) -> str:
    """Blocking: clone SAM and compile it into ``<data>/vectoria/SAM/sam`` (needs git and a C compiler)."""
    home = sam_home(data_dir)
    cc = shutil.which("cc") or shutil.which("gcc") or shutil.which("clang")
    if not cc:
        raise RenderError("no C compiler (on a Mac: xcode-select --install; on Linux: install gcc)")
    if (home / ".git").is_dir():
        subprocess.run(["git", "-C", str(home), "pull", "--ff-only", "-q"], capture_output=True, timeout=120)
    else:
        shutil.rmtree(home, ignore_errors=True)
        home.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        _run(["git", "clone", "-q", "--depth", "1", SAM_REPO, str(home)], timeout=180)
    sources = sorted(str(p) for p in (home / "src").glob("*.c"))
    # -fcommon: SAM defines globals in headers; modern compilers default to -fno-common. No SDL needed for -wav.
    _run([cc, "-O2", "-fcommon", "-w", "-o", str(home / "sam"), *sources], timeout=300)
    speak(str(home / "sam"), "Vectoria is alive.", {})
    return str(home / "sam")


def speak(binary: str, text: str, voice: dict) -> bytes:
    """Blocking: one line through SAM, as 8-bit mono 22050 Hz WAV bytes."""
    said = sayable(text)
    if not any(ch.isalnum() for ch in said):
        raise RenderError(f"nothing speakable in {text!r}")
    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix="vectoria-sam-") as d:
        out = os.path.join(d, "line.wav")
        _run([binary, "-pitch", str(voice.get("pitch", 40)), "-speed", str(voice.get("speed", 72)),
              "-mouth", str(voice.get("mouth", 150)), "-throat", str(voice.get("throat", 155)), "-wav", out, said],
             timeout=30)
        if not os.path.isfile(out) or os.path.getsize(out) < 100:
            raise RenderError("SAM made no sound")
        return Path(out).read_bytes()


# -- lip-sync ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
def load_audio(path: str) -> array:
    """Any audio ffmpeg reads -> mono 16-bit samples at 22050 Hz."""
    p = _run(["ffmpeg", "-v", "error", "-i", path, "-ac", "1", "-ar", str(SAMPLE_RATE), "-f", "s16le", "pipe:1"])
    samples = array("h")
    samples.frombytes(p.stdout[: len(p.stdout) // 2 * 2])
    return samples


def frame_rms(samples: array, fps: int = FPS) -> list:
    step = int(SAMPLE_RATE / fps)
    out = []
    for i in range(0, max(1, len(samples)), step):
        chunk = samples[i:i + step]
        out.append(math.sqrt(sum(x * x for x in chunk) / step) / 32768.0 if chunk else 0.0)
    return out


def mouth_track(samples: array, fps: int = FPS, *, hold: int = 2, flap_every: int = 7,
                sensitivity: float = 0.35, floor: float = 0.003) -> list:
    """Mouth open where the voice is loud relative to its own peaks; held a little, and flapping in long runs."""
    rms = frame_rms(samples, fps)
    peak = sorted(rms)[int(0.9 * (len(rms) - 1))] if rms else 0.0
    out, run = [], 0
    for level in rms:
        want = level > max(floor, peak * sensitivity)
        if out and want != out[-1] and run < hold:
            want = out[-1]
        run = run + 1 if out and want == out[-1] else 1
        out.append(want)
    open_run = 0
    for i, is_open in enumerate(out):
        open_run = open_run + 1 if is_open else 0
        if open_run and open_run % flap_every == 0:
            out[i] = False
    return out


def blink_track(frames: int, fps: int = FPS, rng: random.Random | None = None) -> list:
    rng = rng or random.Random()
    out = [False] * frames
    t = int(rng.uniform(1.0, 2.5) * fps)
    while t < frames:
        for i in range(t, min(frames, t + 3)):
            out[i] = True
        t += int(rng.uniform(2.5, 5.0) * fps)
    return out


# -- her face --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
_ASSETS: dict = {}


def assets() -> dict:
    if not _ASSETS:
        _ASSETS.update(json.loads((HERE / "assets.json").read_text(encoding="utf-8")))
    return _ASSETS


def font_dir(data_dir: str) -> str:
    """Press Start 2P (SIL OFL, unmodified, with its licence), written next to her other files once."""
    d = Path(data_dir) / "vectoria" / "fonts"
    ttf = d / "PressStart2P-Regular.ttf"
    if not ttf.is_file():
        d.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        ttf.write_bytes(base64.b64decode(assets()["font"]))
        shutil.copyfile(HERE / "OFL.txt", d / "OFL.txt")
    return str(d)


def backdrop(size: int) -> Image.Image:
    """A dark backdrop with a soft green glow behind her."""
    bg = Image.new("RGB", (size, size), (10, 14, 13))
    glow = Image.new("L", (size, size), 0)
    ImageDraw.Draw(glow).ellipse((-size * 0.15, size * 0.1, size * 1.15, size * 1.25), fill=140)
    glow = glow.filter(ImageFilter.GaussianBlur(max(1, size // 5)))
    return Image.composite(Image.new("RGB", (size, size), (16, 70, 40)), bg, glow)


_FRAMES: dict = {}


def frames(size: int, vhs: bool, strength: float) -> dict:
    """The four sprite frames composited at ``size`` (raw RGB bytes), with the still VHS look baked in once."""
    key = (size, vhs, round(strength, 2))
    if key not in _FRAMES:
        bg = backdrop(size).convert("RGBA")
        out = {}
        for name in FRAME_NAMES:
            sprite = Image.open(io.BytesIO(base64.b64decode(assets()["sprites"][name]))).convert("RGBA")
            canvas = bg.copy()
            canvas.alpha_composite(sprite.resize((size, size), Image.LANCZOS))
            raw = canvas.convert("RGB").tobytes()
            out[name] = style_frame(raw, size, strength) if vhs and strength > 0 else raw
        _FRAMES.clear()  # only one size is in use at a time
        _FRAMES[key] = out
    return _FRAMES[key]


def still_png(size: int = 512) -> bytes:
    bg = backdrop(size).convert("RGBA")
    sprite = Image.open(io.BytesIO(base64.b64decode(assets()["sprites"]["open_closed"]))).convert("RGBA")
    bg.alpha_composite(sprite.resize((size, size), Image.LANCZOS))
    buf = io.BytesIO()
    bg.convert("RGB").save(buf, format="PNG")
    return buf.getvalue()


# -- the VHS look ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
def rate_args(duration: float, max_kb: int, crf: int = 31) -> list:
    """x264 settings that keep the whole file under ``max_kb`` (0 = quality target only)."""
    if max_kb <= 0 or duration <= 0:
        return ["-crf", str(crf)]
    kbps = max(30, int(max_kb * 8 / duration - AUDIO_KBPS * 1.05))
    return ["-crf", str(crf), "-maxrate", f"{kbps}k", "-bufsize", f"{kbps * 2}k"]


def style_frame(raw: bytes, size: int, strength: float) -> bytes:
    """The still part of the VHS look on one frame: soft blur, colour bleed, RGB shift, scanlines, vignette."""
    s = max(0.0, min(strength, 2.0))
    shift, chroma = max(1, round(size / 170 * s)), max(1, round(size / 128 * s))
    period, thick = max(4, round(size / 85)), max(2, round(size / 170))
    dark = round(255 * (1 - 0.32 * min(s, 1.5)))
    mask = Image.new("L", (size, size), 255)
    draw = ImageDraw.Draw(mask)
    for y in range(0, size, period):
        draw.rectangle((0, y, size, y + thick - 1), fill=dark)
    graph = (f"[0:v]gblur=sigma={0.5 + 0.5 * min(s, 1.5):.2f}:steps=1,format=yuv444p,"
             f"chromashift=crh={chroma}:cbh=-{chroma},format=gbrp,rgbashift=rh=-{shift}:bh={shift}[c];"
             "[c][1:v]blend=all_mode=multiply,vignette=angle=PI/5,"
             "eq=contrast=1.08:saturation=1.18:brightness=0.01,format=rgb24[v]")
    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix="vectoria-style-") as d:
        mask_path = os.path.join(d, "scan.png")
        mask.save(mask_path)
        p = _run(["ffmpeg", "-v", "error", "-f", "rawvideo", "-pix_fmt", "rgb24", "-s", f"{size}x{size}",
                  "-i", "pipe:0", "-loop", "1", "-i", mask_path, "-filter_complex", graph, "-map", "[v]",
                  "-frames:v", "1", "-f", "rawvideo", "pipe:1"], input=raw)
    if len(p.stdout) != size * size * 3:
        raise RenderError("the VHS look couldn't be applied")
    return p.stdout


def moving_graph(size: int, strength: float, subtitles: str | None) -> str:
    """What moves, in the encoding pass: a tracking band that drifts and tears, tape noise, then the subtitles."""
    s = max(0.0, min(strength, 2.0))
    band = round(size * 0.05)
    amp = round(size / 70 * s)
    top = f"clip(mod(t*{size * 0.27:.1f}\\,{size + band})-{band}\\,0\\,{size - band})"
    return ";".join([
        "[0:v]split[a][b]",
        f"[b]crop=iw:{band}:0:'{top}'[band]",
        f"[a][band]overlay=x='{amp}*sin(t*37)':y='{top}':eval=frame,format=yuv420p,noise=alls={round(9 * s)}:allf=t+u"
        + (f",{subtitles}" if subtitles else "") + "[v]",
    ])


def _escape(path: str) -> str:
    return path.replace("\\", "\\\\").replace(":", "\\:").replace("'", "\\'")


def _srt_time(t: timedelta) -> str:
    total = int(t.total_seconds())
    return f"{total // 3600:02d}:{total % 3600 // 60:02d}:{total % 60:02d},{t.microseconds // 1000:03d}"


def duration(path: str) -> float:
    p = _run(["ffprobe", "-v", "quiet", "-print_format", "json", "-show_format", path])
    try:
        return float(json.loads(p.stdout)["format"]["duration"])
    except (KeyError, ValueError) as e:
        raise RenderError(f"ffprobe couldn't time {path}") from e


# -- the clip ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
def ready(sam: str | None) -> str:
    """Why a video can't be made right now ("" when it can)."""
    if not shutil.which("ffmpeg") or not shutil.which("ffprobe"):
        return "ffmpeg isn't installed on the bot's computer"
    if not sam:
        return "her voice (SAM) isn't built yet"
    return ""


def render(text: str, *, sam: str, data_dir: str, opts: dict) -> bytes:
    """Blocking: the finished MP4 for ``text`` (already short)."""
    size = max(128, min(int(opts.get("video_size", 512)), 512)) // 2 * 2
    vhs, strength = bool(opts.get("vhs", True)), float(opts.get("vhs_strength", 1.0))
    lines = split_lines(text) or [text]
    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix="vectoria-") as d:
        paths, srt, t = [], [], timedelta()
        for i, line in enumerate(lines):
            if not any(ch.isalnum() for ch in sayable(line)):
                continue
            path = os.path.join(d, f"line{i}.wav")
            Path(path).write_bytes(speak(sam, line, opts))
            end = t + timedelta(seconds=duration(path))
            srt.append(f"{len(srt) + 1}\n{_srt_time(t)} --> {_srt_time(end)}\n{line.upper()}\n")
            paths.append(path)
            t = end
        if not paths:
            raise RenderError("nothing to say")
        voice = os.path.join(d, "voice.wav")
        inputs = [a for p in paths for a in ("-i", p)]
        join = "".join(f"[{i}:a]" for i in range(len(paths))) + f"concat=n={len(paths)}:v=0:a=1[a]"
        _run(["ffmpeg", "-v", "error", "-y", *inputs, "-filter_complex", join, "-map", "[a]", voice])
        subs_path = os.path.join(d, "subs.srt")
        Path(subs_path).write_text("\n".join(srt), encoding="utf-8")

        mouth = mouth_track(load_audio(voice))
        blinks = blink_track(len(mouth))
        faces = frames(size, vhs, strength)
        seq = [faces[f"{'blink' if b else 'open'}_{'talk' if m else 'closed'}"] for m, b in zip(mouth, blinks)]

        subs = None
        if opts.get("subtitles", True):
            subs = (f"subtitles='{_escape(subs_path)}':fontsdir='{_escape(font_dir(data_dir))}'"
                    f":force_style='{SUBTITLE_STYLE}'")
        if vhs and strength > 0:
            maps = ["-filter_complex", moving_graph(size, strength, subs), "-map", "[v]", "-map", "1:a:0",
                    "-af", "highpass=f=90,lowpass=f=6500,acompressor=threshold=0.25:ratio=3,volume=1.4"]
        else:
            maps = ["-map", "0:v:0", "-map", "1:a:0", *(["-vf", subs] if subs else [])]
        out = os.path.join(d, "vectoria.mp4")
        cmd = ["ffmpeg", "-v", "error", "-y", "-f", "rawvideo", "-pix_fmt", "rgb24", "-s", f"{size}x{size}",
               "-r", str(FPS), "-i", "pipe:0", "-i", voice, *maps, "-c:v", "libx264", "-preset", "veryfast",
               *rate_args(duration(voice), int(opts.get("max_kb", 450))), "-pix_fmt", "yuv420p",
               "-c:a", "aac", "-ac", "1", "-b:a", f"{AUDIO_KBPS}k", "-shortest", "-movflags", "+faststart", out]
        _run(cmd, input=b"".join(seq), timeout=300)
        return Path(out).read_bytes()
